## Lecture slides

All fifteen decks, in teaching order. Every deck opens as a full-screen
presentation — press `?` inside it for navigation shortcuts.

```{=html}
<div class="mp-grid">

  <div class="mp-card is-slide">
    <span class="mp-card-kicker">1 · Introduction</span>
    <h3 class="mp-card-title"><a href="slides/00-introduction/00-introduction.html">Introduction. Organisation. Setup.</a></h3>
    <p class="mp-card-desc">How the course runs, software setup, and the two ideas everything rests on: ceteris paribus and selection bias.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mp-card is-slide">
    <span class="mp-card-kicker">2 · Data wrangling</span>
    <h3 class="mp-card-title"><a href="slides/50-data-wrangling/workflow-tidy-data-wrangling.html">Workflow, tidy data, wrangling</a></h3>
    <p class="mp-card-desc">The data-analysis workflow and what makes a dataset tidy.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mp-card is-slide">
    <span class="mp-card-kicker">2 · Data wrangling</span>
    <h3 class="mp-card-title"><a href="slides/50-data-wrangling/dplyr.html">Wrangling with dplyr</a></h3>
    <p class="mp-card-desc">Extended version of the workflow deck, with the full dplyr verb set worked through.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mp-card is-slide">
    <span class="mp-card-kicker">2 · Data wrangling</span>
    <h3 class="mp-card-title"><a href="slides/50-data-wrangling/import-data.html">Import data</a></h3>
    <p class="mp-card-desc">Reading CSV and Excel files with readr and readxl, and cleaning names with janitor.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mp-card is-slide">
    <span class="mp-card-kicker">3 · Describing data</span>
    <h3 class="mp-card-title"><a href="slides/20-data-description/exploring-numeric-data.html">Exploring numerical data</a></h3>
    <p class="mp-card-desc">Distributions, summaries and the plots that reveal them.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mp-card is-slide">
    <span class="mp-card-kicker">3 · Describing data</span>
    <h3 class="mp-card-title"><a href="slides/20-data-description/correlation.html">Correlation</a></h3>
    <p class="mp-card-desc">Correlation types, how to read their strength, and where they mislead.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mp-card is-slide">
    <span class="mp-card-kicker">4 · Simple regression</span>
    <h3 class="mp-card-title"><a href="slides/10-simple-regression/10-simple-regression.html">Simple regression</a></h3>
    <p class="mp-card-desc">One predictor, least squares, and what the coefficients actually mean.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mp-card is-slide">
    <span class="mp-card-kicker">5 · Multiple regression</span>
    <h3 class="mp-card-title"><a href="slides/30-multiple-regression/multiple-regression.html">Multiple linear regression</a></h3>
    <p class="mp-card-desc">Several predictors at once, and holding other things equal in practice.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mp-card is-slide">
    <span class="mp-card-kicker">5 · Multiple regression</span>
    <h3 class="mp-card-title"><a href="slides/30-multiple-regression/linearity.html">Linearity</a></h3>
    <p class="mp-card-desc">Diagnosing non-linearity and fixing it with transformations.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mp-card is-slide">
    <span class="mp-card-kicker">5 · Multiple regression</span>
    <h3 class="mp-card-title"><a href="slides/30-multiple-regression/ovb.html">Omitted variable bias</a></h3>
    <p class="mp-card-desc">What leaving a variable out does to the estimates you keep.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mp-card is-slide">
    <span class="mp-card-kicker">5 · Multiple regression</span>
    <h3 class="mp-card-title"><a href="slides/30-multiple-regression/collinearity.html">Collinearity</a></h3>
    <p class="mp-card-desc">When predictors carry the same information, and how to detect it.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mp-card is-slide">
    <span class="mp-card-kicker">5 · Multiple regression</span>
    <h3 class="mp-card-title"><a href="slides/30-multiple-regression/heteroscedasticity.html">Heteroscedasticity</a></h3>
    <p class="mp-card-desc">Non-constant error variance, its consequences, and robust standard errors.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mp-card is-slide">
    <span class="mp-card-kicker">5 · Multiple regression</span>
    <h3 class="mp-card-title"><a href="slides/30-multiple-regression/hedonic-regression.html">Hedonic prices model</a></h3>
    <p class="mp-card-desc">A full applied example: decomposing prices into the value of characteristics.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mp-card is-slide">
    <span class="mp-card-kicker">6 · Panel regression</span>
    <h3 class="mp-card-title"><a href="slides/40-panel-regression/panel-regression.html">Panel regression analysis</a></h3>
    <p class="mp-card-desc">Fixed and random effects, and what repeated observations buy you.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mp-card is-slide">
    <span class="mp-card-kicker">7 · Instrumental variables</span>
    <h3 class="mp-card-title"><a href="slides/60-iv/iv.html">Instrumental variable</a></h3>
    <p class="mp-card-desc">Identification when a regressor is endogenous, and the returns-to-schooling example.</p>
  </div>

</div>
```

## How the materials are labelled

The same icons are used in the sidebar and on every topic page:

| Icon | Material |
|:--:|:--|
| 🖥 | Lecture slides — a revealjs deck, opens full screen |
| 📋 | Application exercise — a rendered R walkthrough |
| 📦 | Project bundle — a downloadable RStudio project with data |
| 📺 | Video recording |
| 📖 | Reading or cheat sheet |

## About this site

This site collects the lecture slides, R application exercises and
supplementary materials developed for **MP223 Applied Econometric Methods for
the Social Sciences** at JLU Giessen, Summer Semester 2022. It does not replace
the [Ilias](https://ilias.uni-giessen.de/goto.php?target=crs_301421&client_id=JLUG)
or [StudIP](https://studip.uni-giessen.de/dispatch.php/course/details?sem_id=b1775c5097d2a85c2986b7667d22c3dc&again=yes)
course pages — it makes the slides and code accessible, downloadable and
readable on any device.

Written and taught by **[Eduard (Eddie) Bukin](https://ebukin.github.io)** —
applied economist and open-source data scientist. All materials are open
source and available [on GitHub](https://github.com/EBukin/mp223-2022-aem-R-public/).
